evidence.quote: In pre- paring our improved catalyst we employ a mixture of zinc oxide and ferric hydroxide.
The amount of ferric hydroxide may vary Irom 3% to 25% of the weight of zinc oxide, though we prefer to use about 10%.

props.note: The patent does not know the structure of the working catalyst: the ferric hydroxide is reduced in the synthesis gas.

ferric_hydroxide_preferred.basis: of the weight of zinc oxide

props.name: zinc oxide alone inactive, ferric hydroxide alone inhibiting

evidence.quote: Zine oxide—per se—has no catalytic effect
on the methanol reaction, while ferric hy- droxide—per se—has a positive inhibiting
effect. Nevertheless, when these two in- gredients are properly coinpounded a desir- able methanol catalyst is produced.

props.statement: Zinc oxide by itself has no catalytic effect on the methanol reaction and ferric hydroxide by itself has a positive inhibiting effect; properly compounded together they give a desirable methanol catalyst.

props.name: synthesis carried out with a mixture of CO and CO2

evidence.quote: bon monoxide and pure carbon dioxide are both difficult to obtain economically, so that the methanol synthesis is carried out by reacting a mixture of carbon monoxide and

props.statement: Because pure carbon monoxide and pure carbon dioxide are both difficult to obtain economically, the methanol synthesis is carried out by reacting a mixture of carbon monoxide and carbon dioxide with hydrogen; with carbon dioxide one molecule of water forms per molecule of methanol.

props.statement: When carbon oxides with excess hydrogen are passed over metallic oxides at a pressure above 100 atmospheres and a temperature above 250 °C some reaction nearly always occurs; its extent depends to some degree on space velocity, temperature and pressure, and the products depend almost entirely on the nature and activity of the catalyst.

props.name: iron's hydrogenating effect kept, methane formation inhibited

evidence.quote: We have now discovered a method of em- ploying iron in a methanol] catalyst whereby the desirable hydrogenating catalytic ‘effect
of the iron is obtained and the tendency
to methane formation 1S Inhibited.

props.statement: In the patented catalyst (zinc oxide and ferric hydroxide) the hydrogenating catalytic effect of iron is obtained and the tendency to methane formation is inhibited.

props.name: iron poisons methanol catalysts (literature)

evidence.quote: Without exception the literature on the high pressure catalytic process for synthe- |
sizing methanol definitely states that the presence of iron or any-of its compounds in a catalyst destroys or poisons the catalysts and
The normal effect of the presence of iron in a methanol catalyst is
to cause the reaction of hydrogen and carbon oxides to produce only methane.

props.note: cited from the prior literature, on which the patent's argument depends
props.statement: The literature on the high-pressure methanol synthesis states that the presence of iron or any of its compounds in a catalyst destroys or poisons the catalyst and inhibits methanol formation; iron in some forms reacts with carbon monoxide and the synthesis gas to form a volatile carbonyl compound, and its normal effect is to produce only methane.

props.method: precipitation of ferric hydroxide from ferric nitrate solution with ammonium hydroxide in a hot suspension of zinc oxide; filtering, washing, drying, granulating
steps: 313 grams of ferric nitrate (Fe(NO3)3.9H2O) is dissolved in 25 liters of water which is then heated to 95° C.
to the hot solution is added 750 grams of zinc oxide with stirring
190 cubic centimeters of 12.38 normal ammonium hydroxide is added to precipitate the iron to the hydroxide form
the mixture is allowed to stand, the supernatant liquid siphoned off, and the mass is filtered and washed until there is no test for nitrates in the filtrate
the mass is then completely dried and broken up into granules
